1 · Content
0 characters
Reads the rosters Name Picker and Class Roster Hub already saved on this machine — nothing is uploaded, and nothing here changes them.
{name} becomes the student's name (URL-encoded), {roster} the roster's name, and {n} their position on the list.
Each line becomes one code: label, link or text (comma- or tab-separated, matching how a spreadsheet column pastes in). No delimiter on a line? The whole line is used as both the label and the QR content.
Prints as a plain grid on regular paper — turn on cut lines below if you plan to cut the codes apart with scissors.

Point a camera at any QR code, or upload a photo of one, to see what it contains — a returned library book, a piece of lab equipment, or someone else's printed code. This reads any code, not just ones made by this tool.

Printed under the code in every download and printout — a plain-language fallback for anyone whose camera can't scan it, or a place to spell out a Wi-Fi password beside the code.
Higher levels tolerate more smudging, glare, or a center logo, at the cost of a denser pattern.
